bullets.title: Nebula Mars II
bullets.note: For the last two years, I’ve gotten rid of all TVs at home and experimented with various projectors. The Nebula Mars II was recommended to me by rockstar hotelier and entrepreneur [Liz Lambert](https://el2.convertkit-mail2.com/c/lmun74z88amhk8d82/8mtqhoh0kplrxk/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy8yMDE4LzA2LzE0L2xpei1sYW1iZXJ0Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWNvbnZlcnRraXQmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1jb252ZXJ0a2l0JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj01YmY=). The design is beautiful, and some of the features are fantastic: 1) You can point it at a wall from nearly any angle or distance, and it will autocorrect the aspect ratio and focus; 2) It holds its charge for four hours, so you can use it without an outlet, even outside (or, as I do, on a coffee table); 3) It has excellent built-in speakers; and 4) No cabled laptop required, as it has direct access to most major streaming services. My two main criticisms are 1) I found their online/chat customer service to be very subpar, and 2) the picture can seem quite dim compared to other brighter—but less convenient—projectors I’ve tested and enjoyed. Other specs: 720p, 150” HD picture, dual 10W speakers.

bullets.title: Ten Lessons I Learned While Teaching Myself to Code
bullets.creator: Clive Thompson, an outstanding author and long-form journalist
bullets.note: , an outstanding author and long-form journalist. I particularly enjoyed his section on automation. Here’s a teaser: “‘Don’t learn to code, learn to automate,’ writes the coder Erik Dietrich. This is bang on. Nearly every white-collar job on the planet involves tons of work that can be done more efficiently if you know a _bit_ of coding.”
